response.sql:
WITH item_town AS (
  SELECT ili.order_item_id, c.town_city AS town,
         AVG(ili.product_price) AS avg_price,
         AVG(CAST(ili.derived_product_cost AS REAL) / NULLIF(ili.derived_total_cost, 0)) AS avg_ratio
  FROM Invoice_Line_Items ili
  JOIN Order_Items oi ON oi.order_item_id = ili.order_item_id
  JOIN Orders o ON o.order_id = oi.order_id
  JOIN Customers c ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id
  WHERE c.town_city IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY ili.order_item_id, c.town_city
),
town_avg AS (
  SELECT town, AVG(avg_price) AS avg_price, AVG(avg_ratio) AS avg_ratio
  FROM item_town
  GROUP BY town
),
overall AS (
  SELECT AVG(avg_ratio) AS overall_ratio FROM town_avg
)
SELECT t.town, t.avg_price, t.avg_ratio, t.avg_ratio - o.overall_ratio AS ratio_excess
FROM town_avg t
CROSS JOIN overall o
WHERE t.avg_ratio > o.overall_ratio;

assumptions.assumption: Town means the Customers.town_city value reached via Orders.customer_id; line items whose customer has a NULL town are excluded.

The ratio is computed per line as derived_product_cost / derived_total_cost, and a line with a NULL operand or a zero denominator yields a NULL ratio that AVG skips; the cast to REAL avoids integer division.
The cross-town average is the unweighted mean of the per-town average ratios over all towns (not only those above it), so each town counts equally regardless of how many items it has.
